Command: Get-ChildItem (Shell: powershell, Category: filesystem) Description: Lists files and directories in one or more specified locations Syntax: Get-ChildItem [-Path] <string> [-Recurse] [-Filter <string>] Examples: Get-ChildItem -Recurse -Filter *.txt (Find all .txt files recursively) | gci | Where-Object {$_.Length -gt 1MB} (Find files larger than 1MB) Tags: list, directory, files, ls, dir

Command: Get-Content (Shell: powershell, Category: filesystem) Description: Gets the content of the item at the specified location Syntax: Get-Content [-Path] <string> [-Tail <int>] [-Wait] Examples: Get-Content server.log -Tail 50 (Read last 50 lines of file) | Get-Content data.json | ConvertFrom-Json (Read and parse JSON) Tags: read, view, cat, tail, content

Command: Set-Content (Shell: powershell, Category: filesystem) Description: Writes or replaces the content in an item with new content Syntax: Set-Content [-Path] <string> [-Value] <Object> Examples: Set-Content -Path note.txt -Value 'Hello World' (Overwrite file with text) Tags: write, overwrite, save

Command: Add-Content (Shell: powershell, Category: filesystem) Description: Appends content to the specified items and files Syntax: Add-Content [-Path] <string> [-Value] <Object> Examples: Add-Content -Path app.log -Value 'Task finished at $(Get-Date)' (Append timestamp to log) Tags: append, log, write

Command: Clear-Content (Shell: powershell, Category: filesystem) Description: Deletes the contents of an item without deleting the item itself Syntax: Clear-Content [-Path] <string> Examples: Clear-Content cache.log (Truncate file to 0 bytes) Tags: truncate, clear, empty

Command: New-Item (Shell: powershell, Category: filesystem) Description: Creates a new item such as a file or directory Syntax: New-Item [-Path] <string> [-ItemType <string>] [-Value <Object>] Examples: New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path ./src/components (Create directory tree) | New-Item -ItemType File -Path config.env -Value 'PORT=8000' (Create file with initial value) Tags: create, mkdir, touch, folder, file

Command: Copy-Item (Shell: powershell, Category: filesystem) Description: Copies an item from one location to another Syntax: Copy-Item [-Path] <string> [-Destination] <string> [-Recurse] Examples: Copy-Item -Path ./data -Destination ./backup -Recurse (Copy directory recursively) Tags: copy, duplicate, backup

Command: Move-Item (Shell: powershell, Category: filesystem) Description: Moves an item from one location to another Syntax: Move-Item [-Path] <string> [-Destination] <string> [-Force] Examples: Move-Item *.csv ./archive/ (Move all CSV files to archive) Tags: move, relocate, rename

Command: Remove-Item (Shell: powershell, Category: filesystem) Description: Deletes the specified items and files Syntax: Remove-Item [-Path] <string> [-Recurse] [-Force] Examples: Remove-Item -Path ./temp/*.tmp -Force (Delete temporary files) Tags: delete, remove, rm, unlink

Command: Rename-Item (Shell: powershell, Category: filesystem) Description: Renames an item in a PowerShell provider namespace Syntax: Rename-Item [-Path] <string> [-NewName] <string> Examples: Rename-Item report_old.txt report_new.txt (Rename file) Tags: rename, mv

Command: Test-Path (Shell: powershell, Category: filesystem) Description: Determines whether all elements of a path exist Syntax: Test-Path [-Path] <string> [-PathType <string>] Examples: Test-Path C:\Windows\System32 (Check if folder exists) | if (Test-Path .env) { gc .env } (Read file if present) Tags: exists, check, verify, path

Command: Get-Item (Shell: powershell, Category: filesystem) Description: Gets the item at the specified location Syntax: Get-Item [-Path] <string> Examples: Get-Item package.json | Select-Object Length, LastWriteTime (Get file metadata) Tags: info, stat, metadata

Command: Set-Location (Shell: powershell, Category: filesystem) Description: Sets the current working location to a specified path Syntax: Set-Location [-Path] <string> Examples: Set-Location C:\Projects\orvix_sphere (Change directory) Tags: cd, chdir, navigate

Command: Get-Location (Shell: powershell, Category: filesystem) Description: Gets information about the current working location Syntax: Get-Location Examples: Get-Location (Display current working path) Tags: pwd, cwd, current

Command: Push-Location (Shell: powershell, Category: filesystem) Description: Adds the current location to the top of a location stack Syntax: Push-Location [[-Path] <string>] Examples: Push-Location C:\Temp; ...; Pop-Location (Push location stack) Tags: pushd, stack

Command: Pop-Location (Shell: powershell, Category: filesystem) Description: Changes the current location to the location most recently pushed Syntax: Pop-Location Examples: Pop-Location (Return to previous pushed directory) Tags: popd, return

Command: tree (Shell: cmd, Category: filesystem) Description: Graphically displays the folder structure of a drive or path Syntax: tree [drive:][path] [/F] [/A] Examples: tree /F /A (Display ASCII file hierarchy) Tags: hierarchy, visualize, structure

Command: attrib (Shell: cmd, Category: filesystem) Description: Displays, sets, or removes attributes assigned to files or directories Syntax: attrib [+R|-R] [+A|-A] [+S|-S] [+H|-H] [drive:][path][filename] Examples: attrib +H secret.txt (Mark file as hidden) Tags: attribute, hidden, readonly

Command: compact (Shell: cmd, Category: filesystem) Description: Displays or alters the compression of files on NTFS partitions Syntax: compact [/C | /U] [/S[:dir]] [filename ...] Examples: compact /C /S:C:\Data (Compress directory files) Tags: ntfs, compress, disk

Command: robocopy (Shell: cmd, Category: filesystem) Description: Robust File and Folder Copy for Windows Syntax: robocopy <source> <destination> [<file>[ ...]] [<options>] Examples: robocopy C:\src C:\dst /MIR /MT:8 (Mirror directory using 8 threads) Tags: sync, mirror, robust, fast-copy

Command: xcopy (Shell: cmd, Category: filesystem) Description: Copies files and directory trees Syntax: xcopy <source> [<destination>] [/s] [/e] [/y] Examples: xcopy .\src .\dist /E /I /Y (Copy full tree including empty folders) Tags: copy, tree, legacy

Command: takeown (Shell: cmd, Category: permission) Description: Enables an administrator to recover access to a file that was denied Syntax: takeown [/s <computer>] /f <filename> [/r] [/d {y|n}] Examples: takeown /f C:\LockedFolder /r /d y (Take recursive ownership) Tags: ownership, admin, privilege

Command: icacls (Shell: cmd, Category: permission) Description: Displays or modifies discretionary access control lists on files/folders Syntax: icacls <filename> [/grant[:r] <Sid:perm>[...]] Examples: icacls app.exe /grant Users:(RX) (Grant Read and Execute permissions) Tags: permissions, acl, security

Command: Get-Acl (Shell: powershell, Category: permission) Description: Gets the security descriptor for a resource, such as a file or registry key Syntax: Get-Acl [[-Path] <string>] Examples: Get-Acl .\database.sqlite | Format-List (Display NTFS permissions) Tags: permissions, security, ntfs, audit

Command: Set-Acl (Shell: powershell, Category: permission) Description: Changes the security descriptor of a specified resource Syntax: Set-Acl [-Path] <string> [-AclObject] <Object> Examples: Set-Acl -Path file.txt -AclObject $acl (Apply security descriptor) Tags: permissions, security, apply

Command: Set-ExecutionPolicy (Shell: powershell, Category: permission) Description: Changes the user preference for the Windows PowerShell execution policy Syntax: Set-ExecutionPolicy [-ExecutionPolicy] <string> [-Scope <string>] Examples: Set-ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned -Scope CurrentUser (Allow local unsigned scripts) Tags: policy, scripts, ps1, security

Command: Get-ExecutionPolicy (Shell: powershell, Category: permission) Description: Gets the execution policies for the current session Syntax: Get-ExecutionPolicy [-List] Examples: Get-ExecutionPolicy -List (View execution policy scopes) Tags: policy, audit, security

Command: dir (Shell: cmd, Category: filesystem) Description: Displays a list of files and subdirectories in a directory Syntax: dir [drive:][path][filename] [/o[[:]sortorder]] [/s] Examples: dir /s /b *.log (List all log files recursively in bare format) Tags: list, cmd, files

Command: type (Shell: cmd, Category: filesystem) Description: Displays the contents of a text file Syntax: type [drive:][path]filename Examples: type config.ini (Print contents of config.ini) Tags: view, print, display

Command: more (Shell: cmd, Category: text) Description: Displays output one screen at a time Syntax: more [filename] | command | more Examples: type large.txt | more (Paginate text output) Tags: page, view, paginate

Command: Select-String (Shell: powershell, Category: search) Description: Finds text in strings and files using regular expressions Syntax: Select-String [-Pattern] <string[]> [-Path <string[]>] [-CaseSensitive] Examples: Select-String -Path *.py -Pattern 'def process_' (Search Python files for function definitions) | Get-Content server.log | Select-String 'ERROR' -Context 2 (Find errors with 2 lines context) Tags: grep, search, regex, find

Command: findstr (Shell: cmd, Category: search) Description: Searches for strings in files Syntax: findstr [/s] [/i] [/r] <strings> [filename...] Examples: findstr /s /i /c:"connection failed" *.log (Search text across all logs) Tags: grep, search, cmd

Command: where.exe (Shell: cmd, Category: search) Description: Locates and displays the path of programs matching given pattern Syntax: where [/r <dir>] <pattern> Examples: where node (Locate node.exe on PATH) | where /r C:\ProgramFiles python.exe (Search directory tree for executable) Tags: which, locate, binary, path

Command: Get-Command (Shell: powershell, Category: search) Description: Gets all commands installed on the computer Syntax: Get-Command [[-Name] <string[]>] [-Module <string[]>] Examples: Get-Command *Network* (Find all network cmdlets) | Get-Command python | Select-Object Source (Resolve binary source location) Tags: which, cmdlet, lookup

Command: Get-FileHash (Shell: powershell, Category: search) Description: Computes the hash value for a file by using a specified hash algorithm Syntax: Get-FileHash [-Path] <string[]> [-Algorithm <string>] Examples: Get-FileHash setup.exe -Algorithm SHA256 (Verify SHA256 checksum) Tags: sha256, checksum, integrity, hash

Command: CertUtil (Shell: cmd, Category: search) Description: Dump and display certification authority configuration and hash files Syntax: CertUtil -hashfile <file> [<algorithm>] Examples: certutil -hashfile app.zip MD5 (Calculate MD5 hash) Tags: hash, md5, sha256, crypto

Command: Resolve-Path (Shell: powershell, Category: search) Description: Resolves the wildcard characters in a path and displays the path contents Syntax: Resolve-Path [-Path] <string[]> Examples: Resolve-Path ~\Documents (Expand relative or home path to full path) Tags: absolute, expand, path

Command: Split-Path (Shell: powershell, Category: search) Description: Returns the specified part of a path Syntax: Split-Path [-Path] <string> [-Leaf | -Parent | -Extension] Examples: Split-Path C:\Folder\file.txt -Leaf (Get filename 'file.txt') | Split-Path C:\Folder\file.txt -Parent (Get parent folder) Tags: dirname, basename, path

Command: Join-Path (Shell: powershell, Category: search) Description: Combines a path and a child-path into a single path Syntax: Join-Path [-Path] <string> [-ChildPath] <string> Examples: Join-Path $env:TEMP 'output.log' (Construct platform-safe path) Tags: combine, path, join

Command: find (Shell: cmd, Category: search) Description: Searches for a text string in a file or files Syntax: find [/v] [/c] [/n] [/i] "string" [[drive:][path]filename[ ...]] Examples: find /i "success" results.txt (Case-insensitive text find) Tags: search, text, match

Command: Get-Help (Shell: powershell, Category: search) Description: Displays information about PowerShell commands and concepts Syntax: Get-Help [-Name] <string> [-Full | -Examples] Examples: Get-Help Get-Process -Examples (Show usage examples for cmdlet) Tags: help, documentation, man

Command: Get-Member (Shell: powershell, Category: search) Description: Gets the properties and methods of objects Syntax: Get-Member [[-Name] <string[]>] [-InputObject <psobject>] Examples: Get-Process | Get-Member -MemberType Property (Inspect object properties) Tags: reflect, properties, inspect

Command: Select-Object (Shell: powershell, Category: text) Description: Selects objects or object properties Syntax: Select-Object [[-Property] <Object[]>] [-First <int>] [-Last <int>] [-Unique] Examples: Get-Process | Select-Object -First 10 -Property Name, CPU (Top 10 processes by columns) Tags: filter, columns, slice

Command: Where-Object (Shell: powershell, Category: text) Description: Selects objects from a collection based on their property values Syntax: Where-Object [-FilterScript] <scriptblock> Examples: Get-Service | Where-Object {$_.Status -eq 'Running'} (Filter running services) Tags: filter, predicate, query

Command: ForEach-Object (Shell: powershell, Category: text) Description: Performs an operation against each item in a collection of input objects Syntax: ForEach-Object [-Process] <ScriptBlock[]> Examples: 1..5 | ForEach-Object { $_ * 2 } (Transform each item) Tags: iterate, map, loop

Command: Sort-Object (Shell: powershell, Category: text) Description: Sorts objects by property values Syntax: Sort-Object [[-Property] <Object[]>] [-Descending] [-Unique] Examples: Get-ChildItem | Sort-Object Length -Descending (Sort files by size descending) Tags: order, sort, ranking

Command: Measure-Object (Shell: powershell, Category: text) Description: Calculates the numeric properties of objects, and characters, words, and lines in string objects Syntax: Measure-Object [[-Property] <string[]>] [-Sum] [-Average] [-Line] [-Word] [-Character] Examples: Get-Content code.py | Measure-Object -Line (Count lines of code) | gci | Measure-Object Length -Sum (Calculate total folder bytes) Tags: count, wc, sum, stats

Command: Group-Object (Shell: powershell, Category: text) Description: Groups objects that contain the same value for specified properties Syntax: Group-Object [[-Property] <Object[]>] [-NoElement] Examples: Get-ChildItem | Group-Object Extension (Count files by file extension) Tags: group, aggregate, stats

Command: Out-File (Shell: powershell, Category: text) Description: Sends output to a file Syntax: Out-File [-FilePath] <string> [-Encoding <string>] [-Append] Examples: Get-Process | Out-File -FilePath proc.txt -Encoding utf8 (Save output to UTF-8 file) Tags: save, redirect, export

Command: Tee-Object (Shell: powershell, Category: text) Description: Saves command output in a file or variable and also sends it down the pipeline Syntax: Tee-Object [-FilePath <string>] [-Append] Examples: ping 8.8.8.8 | Tee-Object ping.log (Stream output to console and file) Tags: tee, pipe, log

Command: Out-String (Shell: powershell, Category: text) Description: Converts the objects that PowerShell manages into an array of strings Syntax: Out-String [-InputObject <psobject>] [-Width <int>] Examples: Get-Process | Out-String (Render structured object as single text string) Tags: convert, string, render

Command: ConvertFrom-Json (Shell: powershell, Category: text) Description: Converts a JSON-formatted string to a custom object or a hash table Syntax: ConvertFrom-Json [-InputObject] <string> [-AsHashtable] Examples: Get-Content package.json | ConvertFrom-Json (Parse JSON file) Tags: json, deserialize, parse

Command: ConvertTo-Json (Shell: powershell, Category: text) Description: Converts an object to a JSON-formatted string Syntax: ConvertTo-Json [-InputObject] <Object> [-Depth <int>] Examples: Get-Service | Select -First 3 | ConvertTo-Json (Serialize object as JSON) Tags: json, serialize, export

Command: ConvertFrom-Csv (Shell: powershell, Category: text) Description: Converts object properties in comma-separated value (CSV) format into objects Syntax: ConvertFrom-Csv [-InputObject] <string[]> Examples: Get-Content data.csv | ConvertFrom-Csv (Parse CSV) Tags: csv, table, data

Command: Export-Csv (Shell: powershell, Category: text) Description: Converts objects into a series of CSV strings and saves them in a file Syntax: Export-Csv -Path <string> [-NoTypeInformation] Examples: Get-Process | Export-Csv processes.csv -NoTypeInformation (Export process table to CSV) Tags: csv, export, spreadsheet

Command: Import-Csv (Shell: powershell, Category: text) Description: Creates table-like custom objects from the items in a CSV file Syntax: Import-Csv [-Path] <string[]> Examples: $users = Import-Csv users.csv (Load CSV data into object array) Tags: csv, import, load

Command: Format-Table (Shell: powershell, Category: text) Description: Formats the output of a command as a table Syntax: Format-Table [[-Property] <Object[]>] [-AutoSize] Examples: Get-Process | Format-Table Name, Id, WorkingSet64 -AutoSize (Format table with auto column sizing) Tags: table, display, columns

Command: Get-Process (Shell: powershell, Category: process) Description: Gets the processes that are running on the local computer Syntax: Get-Process [[-Name] <string[]>] [-Id <int[]>] Examples: Get-Process chrome | Select CPU, WorkingSet64 (Get Chrome memory/CPU metrics) | Get-Process | Sort CPU -Descending | Select -First 5 (Top 5 CPU consumers) Tags: ps, tasklist, top, proc

Command: Stop-Process (Shell: powershell, Category: process) Description: Stops one or more running processes Syntax: Stop-Process [-Id] <int[]> [-Force] [-PassThru] Examples: Stop-Process -Name notepad -Force (Kill all notepad processes) | Stop-Process -Id 14204 (Kill process by PID) Tags: kill, terminate, sigkill

Command: Start-Process (Shell: powershell, Category: process) Description: Starts one or more processes on the local computer Syntax: Start-Process [-FilePath] <string> [[-ArgumentList] <string[]>] [-Wait] [-NoNewWindow] Examples: Start-Process notepad.exe config.ini (Launch Notepad with file) | Start-Process python.exe -ArgumentList 'main.py' -NoNewWindow (Run script in background) Tags: launch, exec, open, spawn

Command: Wait-Process (Shell: powershell, Category: process) Description: Waits for the processes to be stopped before accepting more input Syntax: Wait-Process [-Id] <int[]> [-Timeout <int>] Examples: Start-Process build.bat -PassThru | Wait-Process (Wait for build batch to complete) Tags: wait, join, sync

Command: tasklist (Shell: cmd, Category: process) Description: Displays a list of currently running processes on the computer Syntax: tasklist [/s <computer>] [/u <user>] [/m [module]] [/fo {table|list|csv}] Examples: tasklist /fi "STATUS eq running" /fo table (Display running tasks) Tags: ps, processes, cmd

Command: taskkill (Shell: cmd, Category: process) Description: Terminates tasks by process id or image name Syntax: taskkill [/s <computer>] { [/pid <id>] | [/im <image>] } [/f] [/t] Examples: taskkill /f /im node.exe /t (Force kill node process tree) Tags: kill, terminate, tree

Command: Get-Service (Shell: powershell, Category: process) Description: Gets the services on the computer Syntax: Get-Service [[-Name] <string[]>] Examples: Get-Service | Where-Object {$_.Status -eq 'Running'} (List active Windows services) | Get-Service wuauserv (Check Windows Update service status) Tags: service, daemon, status

Command: Start-Service (Shell: powershell, Category: process) Description: Starts one or more stopped services Syntax: Start-Service [-Name] <string[]> Examples: Start-Service -Name Spooler (Start print spooler service) Tags: service, start

Command: Stop-Service (Shell: powershell, Category: process) Description: Stops one or more running services Syntax: Stop-Service [-Name] <string[]> [-Force] Examples: Stop-Service -Name wuauserv (Stop Windows update service) Tags: service, stop

Command: Restart-Service (Shell: powershell, Category: process) Description: Stops and then starts one or more services Syntax: Restart-Service [-Name] <string[]> Examples: Restart-Service -Name LanmanServer (Restart SMB server service) Tags: service, restart, reload

Command: Set-Service (Shell: powershell, Category: process) Description: Starts, stops, and suspends a service, and changes its properties Syntax: Set-Service [-Name] <string> [-StartupType <string>] Examples: Set-Service -Name OpenSSH -StartupType Automatic (Set SSH service to start automatically on boot) Tags: service, startup, boot

Command: Get-CimInstance (Shell: powershell, Category: process) Description: Gets CIM instances from a CIM server using WMI classes Syntax: Get-CimInstance [-ClassName] <string> [-Filter <string>] Examples: Get-CimInstance Win32_Process | Select Name, CommandLine (Inspect process launch arguments) | Get-CimInstance Win32_Processor (Query CPU hardware specs) Tags: wmi, cim, hardware, query

Command: Start-Sleep (Shell: powershell, Category: process) Description: Suspends the activity in a script or session for the specified period Syntax: Start-Sleep [-Seconds] <int> | [-Milliseconds] <int> Examples: Start-Sleep -Seconds 5 (Pause execution for 5 seconds) Tags: delay, pause, timeout, sleep

Command: Get-Job (Shell: powershell, Category: process) Description: Gets PowerShell background jobs that are running in the current session Syntax: Get-Job [[-Id] <int[]>] Examples: Get-Job (List background async jobs) Tags: job, background, async

Command: Start-Job (Shell: powershell, Category: process) Description: Starts a PowerShell background job Syntax: Start-Job [-ScriptBlock] <scriptblock> Examples: Start-Job -ScriptBlock { Get-Process } (Spawn async job in background) Tags: async, spawn, background

Command: Test-NetConnection (Shell: powershell, Category: network) Description: Displays diagnostic information for a connection Syntax: Test-NetConnection [[-ComputerName] <string>] [-Port <int>] Examples: Test-NetConnection google.com -Port 443 (Test TCP handshake to port 443) | Test-NetConnection 127.0.0.1 -Port 8000 (Check local web dashboard port) Tags: ping, port, connect, tcp

Command: Invoke-WebRequest (Shell: powershell, Category: network) Description: Gets content from a web page on the internet Syntax: Invoke-WebRequest [-Uri] <Uri> [-OutFile <string>] [-Method <string>] Examples: Invoke-WebRequest -Uri https://api.github.com/zen -UseBasicParsing (Perform HTTP GET) | iwr -Uri https://example.com/file.zip -OutFile file.zip (Download file) Tags: http, get, curl, download

Command: Invoke-RestMethod (Shell: powershell, Category: network) Description: Sends an HTTP or HTTPS request to a RESTful web service and parses JSON/XML automatically Syntax: Invoke-RestMethod [-Uri] <Uri> [-Method <string>] [-Body <Object>] Examples: Invoke-RestMethod -Uri http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/status (Query Orvix Web API) Tags: rest, api, json, http

Command: Get-NetAdapter (Shell: powershell, Category: network) Description: Gets the basic network adapter properties Syntax: Get-NetAdapter [[-Name] <string[]>] Examples: Get-NetAdapter | Select Name, InterfaceDescription, Status, LinkSpeed (List physical NICs and speeds) Tags: nic, interface, ethernet, wifi

Command: Get-NetIPAddress (Shell: powershell, Category: network) Description: Gets information about IP address configuration Syntax: Get-NetIPAddress [-InterfaceAlias <string>] [-AddressFamily <string>] Examples: Get-NetIPAddress -AddressFamily IPv4 | Select IPAddress, InterfaceAlias (List all local IPv4 addresses) Tags: ip, subnet, dhcp

Command: Resolve-DnsName (Shell: powershell, Category: network) Description: Performs a DNS query resolution for the specified name Syntax: Resolve-DnsName [-Name] <string> [-Type <string>] Examples: Resolve-DnsName google.com -Type A (Resolve DNS A records) Tags: dns, lookup, resolve, host

Command: ping (Shell: cmd, Category: network) Description: Verifies IP-level connectivity to another TCP/IP computer Syntax: ping [-t] [-n <count>] [-l <size>] <target_name> Examples: ping -n 4 8.8.8.8 (Send 4 ICMP echo packets to Google DNS) Tags: icmp, latency, packet-loss

Command: ipconfig (Shell: cmd, Category: network) Description: Displays all current TCP/IP network configuration values Syntax: ipconfig [/all] [/flushdns] [/release] [/renew] Examples: ipconfig /all (Full network adapter diagnostics) | ipconfig /flushdns (Purge DNS resolver cache) Tags: ip, gateway, dns, adapter

Command: netstat (Shell: cmd, Category: network) Description: Displays active TCP connections, ports on which computer is listening, and ethernet statistics Syntax: netstat [-a] [-n] [-o] [-p <proto>] Examples: netstat -ano | findstr :8000 (Find PID listening on port 8000) Tags: ports, connections, sockets

Command: tracert (Shell: cmd, Category: network) Description: Traces the route that network packets take to their destination Syntax: tracert [-d] [-h <maximum_hops>] <target_name> Examples: tracert -d 1.1.1.1 (Trace network hops without DNS lookup) Tags: traceroute, route, latency, hops

Command: nslookup (Shell: cmd, Category: network) Description: Displays information for diagnosing Domain Name System infrastructure Syntax: nslookup [-option] [hostname] [server] Examples: nslookup github.com (Query default DNS server) Tags: dns, domain, nameserver

Command: curl (Shell: cmd, Category: network) Description: Command line tool and library for transferring data with URLs Syntax: curl [options] <url> Examples: curl -s https://icanhazip.com (Fetch public IP address) Tags: http, download, fetch

Command: Get-NetTCPConnection (Shell: powershell, Category: network) Description: Gets information about current TCP connections Syntax: Get-NetTCPConnection [-LocalPort <int[]>] [-State <string[]>] Examples: Get-NetTCPConnection -State Listen | Select LocalAddress, LocalPort, OwningProcess (List listening ports with owning PIDs) Tags: ports, listen, tcp

Command: arp (Shell: cmd, Category: network) Description: Displays and modifies the Address Resolution Protocol cache tables Syntax: arp -a Examples: arp -a (Display IP-to-MAC translation table) Tags: mac, arp, lan

Command: route (Shell: cmd, Category: network) Description: Manipulates network routing tables Syntax: route [-f] [-p] [command [destination] [MASK netmask] [gateway]] Examples: route print (Display IP routing table) Tags: routing, gateway, table

Command: netsh (Shell: cmd, Category: network) Description: Scripting utility to inspect or modify network configuration Syntax: netsh wlan show profiles Examples: netsh wlan show interfaces (View Wi-Fi signal quality and SSID) Tags: wlan, wifi, firewall

Command: Get-NetFirewallRule (Shell: powershell, Category: network) Description: Retrieves firewall rules from the target computer Syntax: Get-NetFirewallRule [-Enabled <string>] [-Direction <string>] Examples: Get-NetFirewallRule -Enabled True | Select -First 5 (Inspect active firewall rules) Tags: firewall, security, ports

Command: Test-Connection (Shell: powershell, Category: network) Description: Sends ICMP echo request packets to one or more computers Syntax: Test-Connection [-TargetName] <string[]> [-Count <int>] Examples: Test-Connection 8.8.8.8 -Count 2 (PowerShell native ICMP ping) Tags: ping, icmp

Command: systeminfo (Shell: cmd, Category: system) Description: Displays detailed configuration information about a computer and its operating system Syntax: systeminfo [/s <computer>] [/fo {TABLE|LIST|CSV}] Examples: systeminfo | findstr /B /C:"OS Name" /C:"OS Version" (Extract OS build) Tags: specs, hardware, os, ram

Command: Get-ComputerInfo (Shell: powershell, Category: system) Description: Gets a consolidated set of system and operating system properties Syntax: Get-ComputerInfo [-Property <string[]>] Examples: Get-ComputerInfo | Select OsName, WindowsVersion, TotalPhysicalMemory (System hardware specs) Tags: specs, ram, os

Command: Get-Volume (Shell: powershell, Category: system) Description: Gets the volume objects on the system Syntax: Get-Volume Examples: Get-Volume | Select DriveLetter, FileSystemType, SizeRemaining, Size (Disk free space on all drives) Tags: disk, storage, drives, free-space

Command: Get-PSDrive (Shell: powershell, Category: system) Description: Gets the drives in the current session Syntax: Get-PSDrive [[-Name] <string[]>] Examples: Get-PSDrive C | Select Used, Free (Get storage stats for drive C:) Tags: drives, storage, filesystem

Command: Get-Date (Shell: powershell, Category: system) Description: Gets the current date and time Syntax: Get-Date [-Format <string>] Examples: Get-Date -Format 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss' (Format timestamp) Tags: time, clock, timestamp, date

Command: dpkg (Shell: bash, Category: package) Description: Package manager for Debian (.deb packages) Syntax: dpkg [options] action Examples: sudo dpkg -i package.deb (Install downloaded .deb file) | dpkg -l | grep python (List installed Python packages) Cross-Platform Equivalent: msiexec Tags: deb, dpkg, debian, install

Command: yum (Shell: bash, Category: package) Description: Yellowdog Updater Modified - package manager for RHEL/CentOS 7 Syntax: yum [options] command Examples: sudo yum install -y epel-release (Install EPEL repo on CentOS) Cross-Platform Equivalent: winget Tags: yum, rpm, rhel, centos

Command: dnf (Shell: bash, Category: package) Description: Dandified YUM - next-generation package manager for Fedora/RHEL 8+ Syntax: dnf [options] command Examples: sudo dnf check-update (Check for available package updates) | sudo dnf install -y htop (Install package) Cross-Platform Equivalent: winget Tags: dnf, fedora, rhel, rpm

Command: pacman (Shell: bash, Category: package) Description: Package manager utility for Arch Linux Syntax: pacman <operation> [options] [targets] Examples: sudo pacman -Syu (Full Arch system rolling upgrade) | sudo pacman -S neovim (Install package) Cross-Platform Equivalent: winget Tags: arch, pacman, packages

Command: snap (Shell: bash, Category: package) Description: Manage cross-distro sandboxed Snap packages Syntax: snap [command] [options] Examples: sudo snap install code --classic (Install VS Code snap) | snap list (List installed snap packages) Cross-Platform Equivalent: winget Tags: snap, sandbox, container, package

Command: flatpak (Shell: bash, Category: package) Description: Build, install and run sandboxed desktop applications Syntax: flatpak [command] [options] Examples: flatpak list (List installed flatpak applications) | flatpak update -y (Update flatpaks) Cross-Platform Equivalent: winget Tags: flatpak, apps, desktop, sandbox

Command: git status (Shell: bash, Category: git) Description: Show the working tree status Syntax: git status [options] Examples: git status (Check modified, staged, and untracked files) | git status -sb (Short status with branch name) Cross-Platform Equivalent: git status Tags: git, vcs, status, changes

Command: git add (Shell: bash, Category: git) Description: Add file contents to the staging index Syntax: git add [options] <pathspec>... Examples: git add . (Stage all current changes) | git add src/main.py (Stage specific file) Cross-Platform Equivalent: git add Tags: git, stage, index

Command: git commit (Shell: bash, Category: git) Description: Record changes to the repository Syntax: git commit [options] Examples: git commit -m 'feat: add terminal controller' (Commit staged changes with message) Cross-Platform Equivalent: git commit Tags: git, commit, save, vcs

Command: git push (Shell: bash, Category: git) Description: Update remote refs along with associated objects Syntax: git push [options] [repository [refspec...]] Examples: git push origin main (Push commits to origin main branch) | git push -u origin feature-branch (Push branch and set upstream) Cross-Platform Equivalent: git push Tags: git, push, remote, sync

Command: git pull (Shell: bash, Category: git) Description: Fetch from and integrate with another repository or a local branch Syntax: git pull [options] [repository [refspec...]] Examples: git pull --rebase origin main (Pull latest changes and rebase cleanly) Cross-Platform Equivalent: git pull Tags: git, pull, fetch, merge

Command: git diff (Shell: bash, Category: git) Description: Show changes between commits, commit and working tree, etc. Syntax: git diff [options] [commit] [--] [path...] Examples: git diff (Show unstaged working tree diff) | git diff --staged (Show changes staged in index) Cross-Platform Equivalent: git diff Tags: git, diff, patch, inspect

Command: git log (Shell: bash, Category: git) Description: Show commit logs Syntax: git log [options] [revision-range] [[--] path...] Examples: git log --oneline -n 10 (Show last 10 commits concisely) | git log --graph --oneline --all (Visual graph of all branches) Cross-Platform Equivalent: git log Tags: git, history, log, commits

Command: git branch (Shell: bash, Category: git) Description: List, create, or delete branches Syntax: git branch [options] [branchname] Examples: git branch -a (List all local and remote branches) | git branch feature-x (Create new branch) Cross-Platform Equivalent: git branch Tags: git, branch, branches

Command: git checkout (Shell: bash, Category: git) Description: Switch branches or restore working tree files Syntax: git checkout [options] <branch> Examples: git checkout main (Switch to main branch) | git checkout -b new-feature (Create and switch to new branch) Cross-Platform Equivalent: git checkout / git switch Tags: git, switch, checkout

Command: git clone (Shell: bash, Category: git) Description: Clone a repository into a new directory Syntax: git clone [options] <repository> [<directory>] Examples: git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/user/repo.git (Fast shallow clone of repository) Cross-Platform Equivalent: git clone Tags: git, clone, download, repo

Command: git reset (Shell: bash, Category: git) Description: Reset current HEAD to the specified state Syntax: git reset [options] [commit] Examples: git reset --soft HEAD~1 (Undo last commit keeping files staged) | git reset --hard HEAD (Discard all local uncommitted changes) Cross-Platform Equivalent: git reset Tags: git, reset, undo, revert

Command: git stash (Shell: bash, Category: git) Description: Stash the changes in a dirty working directory away Syntax: git stash [push|pop|list|drop|clear] Examples: git stash -u (Stash all modified and untracked files) | git stash pop (Restore stashed files) Cross-Platform Equivalent: git stash Tags: git, stash, save, shelf

Command: python3 (Shell: bash, Category: dev) Description: Python 3 interpreter Syntax: python3 [options] [-c cmd | -m mod | file] [arg...] Examples: python3 -m http.server 8080 (Start instant local web server on port 8080) | python3 -c 'import sys; print(sys.version)' (Print Python version) Cross-Platform Equivalent: python Tags: python, script, code, runtime

Command: pip (Shell: bash, Category: dev) Description: The PyPA recommended tool for installing Python packages Syntax: pip <command> [options] Examples: pip install -r requirements.txt (Install project dependencies) | pip list --outdated (Check outdated packages) Cross-Platform Equivalent: pip.exe Tags: python, packages, pip, dependencies

Command: node (Shell: bash, Category: dev) Description: Node.js JavaScript runtime engine Syntax: node [options] [ -e script | script.js ] [arguments] Examples: node index.js (Run JavaScript file) | node -e 'console.log(process.platform)' (Evaluate JS inline) Cross-Platform Equivalent: node.exe Tags: node, javascript, runtime, server

Command: npm (Shell: bash, Category: dev) Description: Node package manager and build tool Syntax: npm <command> [args] Examples: npm install (Install package.json dependencies) | npm run build (Execute build script) | npm run dev (Start dev server) Cross-Platform Equivalent: npm.cmd Tags: npm, node, javascript, packages

Command: make (Shell: bash, Category: dev) Description: GNU make utility to maintain groups of programs from Makefile Syntax: make [options] [target...] Examples: make -j$(nproc) (Parallel build using all available CPU cores) | make clean (Execute clean build target) Cross-Platform Equivalent: make / nmake Tags: build, compile, c, make

Command: gcc (Shell: bash, Category: dev) Description: GNU project C compiler Syntax: gcc [options] file... Examples: gcc -Wall -O2 main.c -o app (Compile C source code into binary) Cross-Platform Equivalent: cl.exe Tags: c, compiler, binary, build

Command: docker (Shell: bash, Category: dev) Description: Manage Docker containers and images Syntax: docker [options] command Examples: docker ps -a (List all running and stopped containers) | docker run -d -p 80:80 nginx (Run nginx container in background) | docker exec -it my_container bash (Interactive bash inside container) Cross-Platform Equivalent: docker.exe Tags: docker, containers, devops, cloud

Command: docker-compose (Shell: bash, Category: dev) Description: Define and run multi-container Docker applications with YAML Syntax: docker-compose [options] [COMMAND] [ARGS...] Examples: docker-compose up -d (Start multi-container stack in background) | docker-compose logs -f (Stream logs from all services) | docker-compose down (Tear down stack) Cross-Platform Equivalent: docker-compose.exe Tags: docker, compose, stack, orchestration

Command: mount (Shell: bash, Category: filesystem) Description: Mount a filesystem to a directory Syntax: mount [options] device dir Examples: sudo mount /dev/sdb1 /mnt/data (Mount drive partition to /mnt/data) | mount | grep ext4 (Show ext4 mounted filesystems) Cross-Platform Equivalent: Mount-DiskImage Tags: mount, drive, storage, filesystem

Command: umount (Shell: bash, Category: filesystem) Description: Unmount file systems Syntax: umount [options] {dir|device}... Examples: sudo umount /mnt/data (Safely unmount partition) Cross-Platform Equivalent: Dismount-DiskImage Tags: unmount, eject, drive

Command: crontab (Shell: bash, Category: scheduling) Description: Maintain crontab files for individual users (scheduled background tasks) Syntax: crontab [options] Examples: crontab -l (List current user scheduled cron jobs) Cross-Platform Equivalent: Get-ScheduledTask Tags: cron, schedule, automation, timer

Command: ffmpeg (Shell: bash, Category: media) Description: Hyper-fast audio and video converter and streamer Syntax: ffmpeg [global_options] {[input_file_options] -i input_url} ... {[output_file_options] output_url} ... Examples: ffmpeg -i input.mp4 -vn -q:a 0 output.mp3 (Extract audio from video as MP3) | ffmpeg -i input.mov -c:v libx264 -crf 23 output.mp4 (Compress video to H.264 MP4) Cross-Platform Equivalent: ffmpeg.exe Tags: video, audio, transcode, media

Command: ffprobe (Shell: bash, Category: media) Description: Multimedia streams analyzer (audio/video metadata) Syntax: ffprobe [options] [input_url] Examples: ffprobe -v quiet -print_format json -show_format -show_streams video.mp4 (Inspect video resolution, codec, and duration in JSON) Cross-Platform Equivalent: ffprobe.exe Tags: media, metadata, duration, resolution

Command: watch (Shell: bash, Category: misc) Description: Execute a program periodically, showing output fullscreen Syntax: watch [options] command Examples: watch -n 1 'nvidia-smi' (Monitor GPU stats every second) | watch -d 'ls -l /tmp' (Watch temporary directory for new files) Cross-Platform Equivalent: while ($true) { ...; Start-Sleep 2 } Tags: loop, monitor, watch, refresh

Command: time (Shell: bash, Category: misc) Description: Time a simple command or give resource usage Syntax: time [options] command [arguments...] Examples: time python heavy_script.py (Measure real, user, and sys CPU execution time) Cross-Platform Equivalent: Measure-Command Tags: benchmark, time, duration, performance

Command: sleep (Shell: bash, Category: misc) Description: Delay for a specified amount of time Syntax: sleep NUMBER[SUFFIX]... Examples: sleep 5 (Pause execution for 5 seconds) | sleep 1m (Sleep for 1 minute) Cross-Platform Equivalent: Start-Sleep -Seconds (sleep) Tags: delay, wait, pause, timer

Command: echo (Shell: bash, Category: text) Description: Display a line of text Syntax: echo [short-option]... [string]... Examples: echo 'Hello World' (Print string to console) | echo 'PATH=$PATH:/opt/bin' >> ~/.bashrc (Append line to bashrc) Cross-Platform Equivalent: Write-Output (echo) Tags: print, output, echo

Command: clear (Shell: bash, Category: misc) Description: Clear the terminal screen Syntax: clear Examples: clear (Clear terminal viewport) Cross-Platform Equivalent: Clear-Host (cls/clear) Tags: terminal, clear, screen

Command: history (Shell: bash, Category: misc) Description: GNU History Library - display shell command history list Syntax: history [n] or history -c Examples: history | tail -n 25 (Show last 25 executed commands) | history | grep docker (Search command history for docker) Cross-Platform Equivalent: Get-History (h) Tags: history, commands, recall, bash

Command: alias (Shell: bash, Category: misc) Description: Define or display aliases Syntax: alias [name[=value] ... ] Examples: alias ll='ls -la' (Create shortcut alias ll) | alias (List all active aliases) Cross-Platform Equivalent: Set-Alias Tags: alias, shortcut, custom

Command: reboot (Shell: bash, Category: power) Description: Reboot the machine Syntax: reboot [options] Examples: sudo reboot (Restart system immediately) Cross-Platform Equivalent: Restart-Computer Tags: reboot, restart, power

Command: shutdown (Shell: bash, Category: power) Description: Power off or halt the machine after a delay Syntax: shutdown [options] [time] [wall...] Examples: sudo shutdown -h now (Shut down machine immediately) | sudo shutdown -c (Cancel scheduled shutdown) Cross-Platform Equivalent: Stop-Computer (shutdown /s) Tags: shutdown, power, off

Command: Get-ChildItem (Shell: powershell, Category: filesystem) Description: Lists files and directories in one or more specified locations Syntax: Get-ChildItem [-Path] <string> [-Recurse] [-Filter <string>] Tags: list, directory, files, ls, dir Examples: Get-ChildItem -Recurse -Filter *.txt (Find all .txt files recursively) | gci | Where-Object {$_.Length -gt 1MB} (Find files larger than 1MB)

Command: Get-Content (Shell: powershell, Category: filesystem) Description: Gets the content of the item at the specified location Syntax: Get-Content [-Path] <string> [-Tail <int>] [-Wait] Tags: read, view, cat, tail, content Examples: Get-Content server.log -Tail 50 (Read last 50 lines of file) | Get-Content data.json | ConvertFrom-Json (Read and parse JSON)

Command: Set-Content (Shell: powershell, Category: filesystem) Description: Writes or replaces the content in an item with new content Syntax: Set-Content [-Path] <string> [-Value] <Object> Tags: write, overwrite, save Examples: Set-Content -Path note.txt -Value 'Hello World' (Overwrite file with text)

Command: Add-Content (Shell: powershell, Category: filesystem) Description: Appends content to the specified items and files Syntax: Add-Content [-Path] <string> [-Value] <Object> Tags: append, log, write Examples: Add-Content -Path app.log -Value 'Task finished at $(Get-Date)' (Append timestamp to log)

Command: Clear-Content (Shell: powershell, Category: filesystem) Description: Deletes the contents of an item without deleting the item itself Syntax: Clear-Content [-Path] <string> Tags: truncate, clear, empty Examples: Clear-Content cache.log (Truncate file to 0 bytes)

Command: Copy-Item (Shell: powershell, Category: filesystem) Description: Copies an item from one location to another Syntax: Copy-Item [-Path] <string> [-Destination] <string> [-Recurse] Tags: copy, duplicate, backup Examples: Copy-Item -Path ./data -Destination ./backup -Recurse (Copy directory recursively)

Command: Move-Item (Shell: powershell, Category: filesystem) Description: Moves an item from one location to another Syntax: Move-Item [-Path] <string> [-Destination] <string> [-Force] Tags: move, relocate, rename Examples: Move-Item *.csv ./archive/ (Move all CSV files to archive)

Command: Remove-Item (Shell: powershell, Category: filesystem) Description: Deletes the specified items and files Syntax: Remove-Item [-Path] <string> [-Recurse] [-Force] Tags: delete, remove, rm, unlink Examples: Remove-Item -Path ./temp/*.tmp -Force (Delete temporary files)

Command: New-Item (Shell: powershell, Category: filesystem) Description: Creates a new item such as a file or directory Syntax: New-Item [-Path] <string> [-ItemType <string>] [-Value <Object>] Tags: create, mkdir, touch, folder, file Examples: New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path ./src/components (Create directory tree) | New-Item -ItemType File -Path config.env -Value 'PORT=8000' (Create file with initial value)

Command: Test-Path (Shell: powershell, Category: filesystem) Description: Determines whether all elements of a path exist Syntax: Test-Path [-Path] <string> [-PathType <string>] Tags: exists, check, verify, path Examples: Test-Path C:\Windows\System32 (Check if folder exists) | if (Test-Path .env) { gc .env } (Read file if present)

Command: Rename-Item (Shell: powershell, Category: filesystem) Description: Renames an item in a PowerShell provider namespace Syntax: Rename-Item [-Path] <string> [-NewName] <string> Tags: rename, mv Examples: Rename-Item report_old.txt report_new.txt (Rename file)

Command: Get-Item (Shell: powershell, Category: filesystem) Description: Gets the item at the specified location Syntax: Get-Item [-Path] <string> Tags: info, stat, metadata Examples: Get-Item package.json | Select-Object Length, LastWriteTime (Get file metadata)
Command: Set-Item (Shell: powershell, Category: filesystem) Description: Changes the value of an item Syntax: Set-Item [-Path] <path> [-Value] <object> Tags: si Examples: Set-Item (Run Set-Item)
Command: Clear-Item (Shell: powershell, Category: filesystem) Description: Clears contents of an item Syntax: Clear-Item [-Path] <path> Tags: cli Examples: Clear-Item (Run Clear-Item)

Command: Split-Path (Shell: powershell, Category: search) Description: Returns the specified part of a path Syntax: Split-Path [-Path] <string> [-Leaf | -Parent | -Extension] Tags: dirname, basename, path Examples: Split-Path C:\Folder\file.txt -Leaf (Get filename 'file.txt') | Split-Path C:\Folder\file.txt -Parent (Get parent folder)

Command: Join-Path (Shell: powershell, Category: search) Description: Combines a path and a child-path into a single path Syntax: Join-Path [-Path] <string> [-ChildPath] <string> Tags: combine, path, join Examples: Join-Path $env:TEMP 'output.log' (Construct platform-safe path)

Command: Resolve-Path (Shell: powershell, Category: search) Description: Resolves the wildcard characters in a path and displays the path contents Syntax: Resolve-Path [-Path] <string[]> Tags: absolute, expand, path Examples: Resolve-Path ~\Documents (Expand relative or home path to full path)

Command: Convert-Path (Shell: powershell, Category: filesystem) Description: Converts provider path to standard Windows path Syntax: Convert-Path [-Path] <path> Tags: path Examples: Convert-Path (Run Convert-Path)

Command: Get-Location (Shell: powershell, Category: filesystem) Description: Gets information about the current working location Syntax: Get-Location Tags: pwd, cwd, current Examples: Get-Location (Display current working path)

Command: Set-Location (Shell: powershell, Category: filesystem) Description: Sets the current working location to a specified path Syntax: Set-Location [-Path] <string> Tags: cd, chdir, navigate Examples: Set-Location C:\Projects\orvix_sphere (Change directory)

Command: Push-Location (Shell: powershell, Category: filesystem) Description: Adds the current location to the top of a location stack Syntax: Push-Location [[-Path] <string>] Tags: pushd, stack Examples: Push-Location C:\Temp; ...; Pop-Location (Push location stack)

Command: Pop-Location (Shell: powershell, Category: filesystem) Description: Changes the current location to the location most recently pushed Syntax: Pop-Location Tags: popd, return Examples: Pop-Location (Return to previous pushed directory)

Command: Get-ItemPropertyValue (Shell: powershell, Category: filesystem) Description: Gets value of a property on an item Syntax: Get-ItemPropertyValue [-Path] <path> [-Name] <prop> Tags: property Examples: Get-ItemPropertyValue (Run Get-ItemPropertyValue)

Command: Set-ItemProperty (Shell: powershell, Category: registry) Description: Creates or changes the value of a property of an item Syntax: Set-ItemProperty [-Path] <string[]> [-Name] <string> [-Value] <Object> Tags: registry, write, configure Examples: Set-ItemProperty 'HKCU:\Software\Orvix' -Name 'Theme' -Value 'Dark' (Set registry configuration value)

Command: Get-ItemProperty (Shell: powershell, Category: registry) Description: Gets the properties of a specified item (registry key or filesystem item) Syntax: Get-ItemProperty [-Path] <string[]> [[-Name] <string[]>] Tags: registry, hkey, startup Examples: Get-ItemProperty 'HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run' (View user startup programs)

Command: New-ItemProperty (Shell: powershell, Category: filesystem) Description: Creates a new property on an item or registry key Syntax: New-ItemProperty [-Path] <path> -Name <string> -PropertyType <type> -Value <val> Tags: registry Examples: New-ItemProperty (Run New-ItemProperty)

Command: Remove-ItemProperty (Shell: powershell, Category: registry) Description: Deletes the property and its value from an item Syntax: Remove-ItemProperty [-Path] <string[]> [-Name] <string[]> Tags: registry, delete Examples: Remove-ItemProperty 'HKCU:\Software\Orvix' -Name 'OldKey' (Remove registry key value)

Command: Clear-ItemProperty (Shell: powershell, Category: filesystem) Description: Clears property value on an item or registry key Syntax: Clear-ItemProperty [-Path] <path> -Name <string> Tags: registry Examples: Clear-ItemProperty (Run Clear-ItemProperty)

Command: Copy-ItemProperty (Shell: powershell, Category: filesystem) Description: Copies property from one item to another Syntax: Copy-ItemProperty [-Path] <src> -Destination <dest> -Name <prop> Tags: registry Examples: Copy-ItemProperty (Run Copy-ItemProperty)

Command: Move-ItemProperty (Shell: powershell, Category: filesystem) Description: Moves property from one item to another Syntax: Move-ItemProperty [-Path] <src> -Destination <dest> -Name <prop> Tags: registry Examples: Move-ItemProperty (Run Move-ItemProperty)

Command: Rename-ItemProperty (Shell: powershell, Category: filesystem) Description: Renames property on an item or registry key Syntax: Rename-ItemProperty [-Path] <path> -Name <old> -NewName <new> Tags: registry Examples: Rename-ItemProperty (Run Rename-ItemProperty)

Command: Get-Process (Shell: powershell, Category: process) Description: Gets the processes that are running on the local computer Syntax: Get-Process [[-Name] <string[]>] [-Id <int[]>] Tags: ps, tasklist, top, proc Examples: Get-Process chrome | Select CPU, WorkingSet64 (Get Chrome memory/CPU metrics) | Get-Process | Sort CPU -Descending | Select -First 5 (Top 5 CPU consumers)

Command: Start-Process (Shell: powershell, Category: process) Description: Starts one or more processes on the local computer Syntax: Start-Process [-FilePath] <string> [[-ArgumentList] <string[]>] [-Wait] [-NoNewWindow] Tags: launch, exec, open, spawn Examples: Start-Process notepad.exe config.ini (Launch Notepad with file) | Start-Process python.exe -ArgumentList 'main.py' -NoNewWindow (Run script in background)

Command: Stop-Process (Shell: powershell, Category: process) Description: Stops one or more running processes Syntax: Stop-Process [-Id] <int[]> [-Force] [-PassThru] Tags: kill, terminate, sigkill Examples: Stop-Process -Name notepad -Force (Kill all notepad processes) | Stop-Process -Id 14204 (Kill process by PID)

Command: Wait-Process (Shell: powershell, Category: process) Description: Waits for the processes to be stopped before accepting more input Syntax: Wait-Process [-Id] <int[]> [-Timeout <int>] Tags: wait, join, sync Examples: Start-Process build.bat -PassThru | Wait-Process (Wait for build batch to complete)

Command: Debug-Process (Shell: powershell, Category: process) Description: Attaches debugger to running process Syntax: Debug-Process [-Id <int>] Tags: debug Examples: Debug-Process (Run Debug-Process)

Command: Get-Service (Shell: powershell, Category: process) Description: Gets the services on the computer Syntax: Get-Service [[-Name] <string[]>] Tags: service, daemon, status Examples: Get-Service | Where-Object {$_.Status -eq 'Running'} (List active Windows services) | Get-Service wuauserv (Check Windows Update service status)

Command: Start-Service (Shell: powershell, Category: process) Description: Starts one or more stopped services Syntax: Start-Service [-Name] <string[]> Tags: service, start Examples: Start-Service -Name Spooler (Start print spooler service)

Command: Stop-Service (Shell: powershell, Category: process) Description: Stops one or more running services Syntax: Stop-Service [-Name] <string[]> [-Force] Tags: service, stop Examples: Stop-Service -Name wuauserv (Stop Windows update service)

Command: Restart-Service (Shell: powershell, Category: process) Description: Stops and then starts one or more services Syntax: Restart-Service [-Name] <string[]> Tags: service, restart, reload Examples: Restart-Service -Name LanmanServer (Restart SMB server service)

Command: Set-Service (Shell: powershell, Category: process) Description: Starts, stops, and suspends a service, and changes its properties Syntax: Set-Service [-Name] <string> [-StartupType <string>] Tags: service, startup, boot Examples: Set-Service -Name OpenSSH -StartupType Automatic (Set SSH service to start automatically on boot)

Command: Suspend-Service (Shell: powershell, Category: service) Description: Suspends (pauses) one or more running services Syntax: Suspend-Service [-Name] <string[]> Tags: pause Examples: Suspend-Service (Run Suspend-Service)

Command: Resume-Service (Shell: powershell, Category: service) Description: Resumes one or more suspended services Syntax: Resume-Service [-Name] <string[]> Tags: resume Examples: Resume-Service (Run Resume-Service)

Command: New-Service (Shell: powershell, Category: service) Description: Creates a new Windows service entry Syntax: New-Service -Name <string> -BinaryPathName <path> Tags: create Examples: New-Service (Run New-Service)

Command: Test-NetConnection (Shell: powershell, Category: network) Description: Displays diagnostic information for a connection Syntax: Test-NetConnection [[-ComputerName] <string>] [-Port <int>] Tags: ping, port, connect, tcp Examples: Test-NetConnection google.com -Port 443 (Test TCP handshake to port 443) | Test-NetConnection 127.0.0.1 -Port 8000 (Check local web dashboard port)

Command: Invoke-WebRequest (Shell: powershell, Category: network) Description: Gets content from a web page on the internet Syntax: Invoke-WebRequest [-Uri] <Uri> [-OutFile <string>] [-Method <string>] Tags: http, get, curl, download Examples: Invoke-WebRequest -Uri https://api.github.com/zen -UseBasicParsing (Perform HTTP GET) | iwr -Uri https://example.com/file.zip -OutFile file.zip (Download file)
